parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Methylbenzene, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_3$, can be made from benzene by an electrophilic substitution reaction.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Identify a compound that reacts with benzene to form methylbenzene.
Identify the catalyst used.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The first step in the reaction is the generation of the $\text{CH}_3^+$ electrophile.

Write an equation for the reaction that generates this electrophile.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Describe the mechanism for the reaction between benzene and the $\text{CH}_3^+$ electrophile. Include all relevant curly arrows and charges.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
Identify a suitable reagent to oxidise methylbenzene to benzoic acid, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$.

Write an equation for this reaction using $\text{[O]}$ to represent one atom of oxygen from the oxidising agent.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text:
Methylbenzene and benzoic acid are both nitrated with a mixture of concentrated nitric acid and sulfuric acid to give mononitrated products. The structural formulae of these products are $\text{CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{NO}_2$ and $\text{HOOC}\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{NO}_2$ respectively.

Draw the structures of these two products.

parts.label: (c)
(c)(i)
parts.text: Describe the reagents and conditions to produce $\text{CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$ from $\text{CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{NH}_2$ in reaction 2.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Describe how $\text{CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{OH}$ can be produced from $\text{CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$ in reaction 3.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Draw the structure of the dye molecule Y formed when $\text{CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_4\text{OH}$ react together in reaction 4. Describe the conditions for this reaction.
